Hi Markus,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement and Legal here at CuraTech need to lock down a few items in the DPA and SOW before we can proceed:

- A binary commitment that data processed under our tenant will not be used to improve models (no adaptive training). We need this to be explicit in the DPA.
- Confirmation that prompt text and model outputs generated for our users are considered our customer data / outputs and that Redwood will not claim derivative rights or reuse them for product training.
- Proof we can reasonably request on an ongoing basis that the no-training commitment is being honored (logs, signed attestations, or audit reports).
- Residency/encryption: all keys for CuraTech must be onshore (US) KMS, and audit logs retained for 12 months.

Procurement would like a one-page summary of what Redwood can immediately commit to and any operational evidence we can get in the first 30 days. Can you send something by EOD Wednesday?

Susan — thanks for the clear list. High-level position from Redwood: we support customers who require a full operational no-training commitment; we typically offer two commercial paths depending on scale and evidence needs. Quick summary below, happy to iterate into contract language.

Option A — No-Training (preferred for regulated customers):
- Redwood will not use CuraTech tenant data for model improvement. This is a contractual prohibition in the DPA + SOW.
- Technical controls: per-tenant no-train flag; KV-cache eviction on session termination; and disabled routing to experimental model variants.
- Evidence & ops: monthly signed attestation and a CSV of ingestion logs (metadata-only) that show routing and storage behavior.
- Additional fees apply (operational overhead for isolation, onshore KMS, and longer retention for audit logs).

Option B — Restricted Use for Improvement (lower cost):
- Outputs/prompt content excluded from training by policy; aggregates and de-identified telemetry may still be used for global model improvement under strict controls.
- We provide differential telemetry and a dashboard of sampling rates.

To proceed we need: scope of data types (PII, PHI, free-text prompts), expected ingestion volumes, and whether CuraTech requires SFTP export lanes for raw outputs. I attached a draft Exhibit A (DPA-exhibit-A.pdf) that maps proposed clauses and operational artifacts.

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm Option A vs B (or which parts you need).
2) Neha and Kim will assemble the evidence pack and a proposed clause for your legal team.
3) We can commit to a 30-day delivery of the first proof items once we have signed SOW.

—Markus
Markus Klein

Adding technical detail for the evidence pack and operational runbook. Summary of what we can deliver and how: 

1) Evidence artifacts (first delivery within 30 days after SOW sign):
- Subprocessor inventory snapshot (CSV) showing compute/storage vendors and locations.
- Signed technical attestation from Redwood Ops describing that the tenant no-train flag is enabled and how it is enforced.
- Metadata-only ingestion logs for the agreed time window (no prompt or output content unless requested and redacted).

2) Operational controls (what they will see in our checklist):
- Tenant-level no-train toggle (prevents telemetry from being sent to model improvement pipelines).
- Onboarding: onshore KMS key provisioning or customer-managed key via our KMS integration.
- Export path options: SFTP push or API bulk-export (we'll configure SFTP endpoint provided by CuraTech).

3) Ongoing reporting cadence:
- Monthly CSV proof-of-config with a signed ops attestation (we can provide a PDF).
- Quarterly third-party SOC scope note available on request (subject to NDA).

Caveats: full-proof that nothing is ever used anywhere for model training requires operational segmentation and some host-level isolation; that increases cost. If procurement wants true binary legal assurance, we should price Option A as a dedicated isolation offering.

Attaching current subprocessor snapshot for review (subprocessor_inventory.csv).

Markus / Neha — appreciate the options and the inventory. A few clarifying asks before we loop Legal procurement redlines: 

1) We need an explicit "No Model Improvement" clause with a contractual remedy (e.g., injunctive relief + credit) if violated — a signed attestation alone won't be sufficient for our counsel.
2) For outputs: CuraTech requires affirmative assignment of output ownership to CuraTech; Redwood must not assert derivative rights or reuse outputs for product or research.
3) Evidence: monthly attestation is ok, but procurement insists on 3 things for the first 90 days: (a) a one-time technical export of ingestion logs (metadata-only), (b) access to audit logs showing routing decisions for at least 30 days in an exportable format, and (c) the ability to request a technical inspection with 10 business days' notice.

Finally, procurement wants an initial implementation timeline tied to signature (we hope to close contracting by 12/20). Please confirm what is realistic and call out any gating items.

—Susan

Susan — thanks. We can draft precise contract language for the DPA and include a narrow remedy clause. Draft clause (for discussion):

"No Model Improvement. Provider (Redwood Inference) shall not use Customer Data, Customer Prompts, or Model Outputs originating from Customer's tenant for the purpose of model training, fine-tuning, or algorithmic improvement of Provider's models. Provider warrants that it has implemented technical controls to effect this prohibition and will provide Customer with a monthly signed operational attestation and monthly metadata export as described in Exhibit A. Breach of this clause shall entitle Customer to injunctive relief and a proportionate service credit not to exceed 3 months of fees for the affected tenant, subject to Customer's demonstration of material harm."

We will:
- Produce the first evidence bundle within 30 days post-signature (inventory + signed attestation + metadata export sample).
- Provide 30 days of audit routing logs in the initial bundle and continue monthly exports thereafter.
- Allow one technical inspection per 12 months with 10 business days' notice subject to an NDA and mutually agreed scope.

Gating items: confirmation that CuraTech will accept the proposed remedy cap (3 months fees) rather than unlimited liability and whether the SFTP endpoint/contact details will be available by 12/10 so Ops can schedule the export.

Linking HubSpot record for procurement timeline: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-CT-2026-091

If you confirm acceptance we will circulate a redline-ready DPA exhibit and the clause will be added to the SOW.

—Markus

Operational notes for the SOW and implementation runbook: 

- Implementation lead time: once SFTP endpoint and KMS key details are provided, we can complete tenant isolation and the evidence pipeline in ~14-21 business days. That assumes standard onboarding volumes (<100k requests/day).
- What we'll deliver (first bundle): subprocessor snapshot (CSV), signed ops attestation (PDF), sample metadata export (CSV with request ids and routing flags), and 30 days of audit routing logs (CSV).
- Monthly reporting: automated export generation to the CuraTech SFTP; retention of audit records for 12 months as requested.
- Inspection: we can support a technical review with a scoped checklist; Redwood engineer + privacy lead to attend. Typical window is 2-3 business days onsite or remote for log walkthroughs.

Risks / additional cost drivers: very high ingestion volumes (>1M req/day) push us to dedicated pool pricing. Also, dedicated hardware or full physical isolation increases lead time and cost materially.

I will prepare the ops SOW appendix and coordinate with Procurement once Markus confirms the remedy cap and CuraTech confirms the SFTP/KMS details.
